protocol.cohort_selection: Sort eligible user IDs; NumPy default_rng(cohort_seed).permutation, take at most max_users; retain every eligible target for those users. Same cases for every objective and cap.
protocol.candidate_set: Full prepared catalog, excluding ALL strictly earlier positive items even when visible history is truncated.
protocol.history: Most recent distinct rating>=4 items with timestamp strictly before the target; cap truncates only model input.
protocol.evaluation: Prequential fixed weights: earlier validation/test feedback can enter a later history; same-time feedback cannot.
protocol.averaging: Within-user target mean, then equal user macro-average; popularity cohorts recompute macro-average within their eligible users.
protocol.popularity: Distinct rating>=4 TRAIN users per item; bins 0,1-5,6-20,21+.
protocol.exposure: Cap20 Top10 slots counted per eligible target (event weighted); coverage denominator is the full prepared catalog, including zero-exposure items.
protocol.bootstrap: Paired user resampling within each cap vs cap20 comparison; conditional on one checkpoint/cohort, not independent training repeats.

limitations: One predeclared seed42 checkpoint per objective/domain and at most1000 test users per domain by default; separate from the original27 full-test records.
Historical rating>=4 events are positive feedback, not natural-language query relevance or explicit negative judgments.
History truncation changes model input at inference; models are not retrained for each cap. The mean-pooling head has no positional history model.
Popularity/coverage/exposure concentration describe this fixed cohort and catalog; coverage is not satisfaction, and low-interaction is not strict cold start.
Bootstrap intervals condition on selected checkpoints/users and do not measure training-seed uncertainty or establish a general fine-tuning gain.
